name: Algeria
tagline: The largest country in Africa, and the emptiest
summary: Four-fifths Sahara, a Mediterranean coast of Roman cities, and the Hoggar and Tassili massifs in the deep south — rock art nine thousand years old on a plateau the size of Britain.
when: October to April. The Sahara is unvisitable in summer and the Tassili needs cool nights.

entries.caption: The Sahara Begins Here
entries.description: Four-fifths of Algeria is desert, and the last fifth holds forty million people.
entries.subject: the dunes of the Grand Erg Oriental in southern Algeria at low sun

entries.caption: Hoggar and Tassili
entries.description: Volcanic spires in the Hoggar, and a sandstone plateau at Tassili n'Ajjer eroded into streets.
entries.subject: the volcanic pinnacles of the Hoggar massif near Tamanrasset

entries.caption: What Lives in the Sand
entries.description: Fennec fox, addax and the last Saharan cheetah, all of them nocturnal and all of them rare.
entries.subject: a fennec fox at the edge of dunes in the Algerian Sahara

entries.caption: Desert Watching, Not Game Driving
entries.description: There is no safari circuit here. You go out at dawn with somebody who reads tracks.
entries.subject: a guide reading animal tracks in sand in the Algerian Sahara

entries.caption: The Djurdjura and the Hoggar
entries.description: Snow on the Djurdjura above Kabylie in winter; Mount Tahat at 2,908 metres in the far south.
entries.subject: snow on the Djurdjura range above the Kabylie valleys

entries.caption: Water in a Dry Country
entries.description: The falls at Kefrida in Bejaia, in a green fold of the coast that surprises everyone.
entries.subject: the Kefrida waterfall falling through green forest in Bejaia province

entries.caption: Chotts and Oases
entries.description: Salt lakes that mirror the sky at Chott Melrhir, and the palmeraie at Timimoun.
entries.subject: the palm oasis and red ksar walls of Timimoun in the Gourara

entries.caption: A Thousand Kilometres of Mediterranean
entries.description: The Turquoise Coast west of Algiers, and the coves at Jijel under limestone cliffs.
entries.subject: a limestone cove on the Jijel coast with clear water

entries.caption: The Kabylie Cedars
entries.description: Atlas cedar on the Djurdjura ridge, some of it four hundred years old.
entries.subject: ancient Atlas cedar trees on the Djurdjura ridge in Kabylie

entries.caption: Crossing the Tassili
entries.description: A week on foot with Tuareg guides among the sandstone towers, sleeping out.
entries.subject: hikers among the sandstone towers of Tassili n'Ajjer

entries.caption: Three Languages Before Lunch
entries.description: Darija, Tamazight and French, and a coastline that has been argued over for three thousand years.
entries.subject: a busy street in the Casbah of Algiers with people talking

entries.caption: The Kabyles and the Tuareg
entries.description: Berber-speaking Kabylie in the north, and the Tuareg of the Hoggar in the far south.
entries.subject: a Tuareg man in indigo tagelmust in the Hoggar

entries.caption: Couscous on Friday
entries.description: Chorba, m'hadjeb, and the Friday couscous that stops the whole country.
entries.subject: a plate of Algerian couscous with vegetables and broth

entries.caption: Yennayer and the Sufi Moussems
entries.description: The Amazigh new year in January, and the moussems that fill desert towns for a week.
entries.subject: dancers at the Amazigh Yennayer new year celebration

entries.caption: Silver, Wool and Pottery
entries.description: Kabyle silver with coral and enamel, Beni Isguen weaving, and the pottery of Maatkas.
entries.subject: Kabyle silver jewellery with coral and enamel on a cloth

entries.caption: Timgad and Djemila
entries.description: Two Roman cities the desert kept: Timgad's grid is complete, Djemila's forum still stands.
entries.subject: the Roman ruins and triumphal arch of Timgad on the high plateau

entries.caption: Seven Sites, Nine Thousand Years
entries.description: Tassili's rock art records a Sahara with rivers in it, and the M'zab valley is still lived in.
entries.subject: prehistoric rock paintings of cattle at Tassili n'Ajjer

entries.caption: Algiers, White on the Bay
entries.description: The Casbah stacked above the harbour, and the boulevards the French cut below it.
entries.subject: the white terraces of the Casbah of Algiers above the bay

entries.caption: The Casbah and the M'zab
entries.description: Ottoman houses on top of each other in Algiers, and five fortified towns in the M'zab built to one plan.
entries.subject: the tiered houses and minaret of Ghardaia in the M'zab valley

entries.caption: Coffee and Argument
entries.description: The cafe is the institution. So is the argument in it.
entries.subject: men at a pavement cafe table in Algiers talking

entries.caption: Beaches and Roman Stones
entries.description: Tipaza has a Roman city on a beach, which solves most family arguments at once.
entries.subject: Roman columns at Tipaza with the Mediterranean behind

entries.caption: Walking the North
entries.description: The Chrea forest above Blida, the Gouraya cliffs at Bejaia, and the Djurdjura ridge.
entries.subject: a walking path along the Gouraya cliffs above Bejaia

entries.caption: Rare, and Getting Less So
entries.description: Restored Ottoman houses in the Casbah, and desert camps in the Hoggar run to a standard.
entries.subject: a restored Ottoman courtyard house in the Casbah of Algiers

entries.caption: The Case for Going Now
entries.description: Algeria takes very few visitors for its size, and everything about it is the better for that.
entries.subject: an empty Roman street at Djemila with nobody on it

entries.caption: Light on Sandstone
entries.description: Tassili at either end of the day, when the rock goes from ochre to red to purple.
entries.subject: sandstone formations at Tassili n'Ajjer in late afternoon light

entries.caption: Ghardaia
entries.description: Five towns in a valley, built by the Mozabites in the eleventh century and still run their way.
entries.subject: the pyramid-stacked town of Ghardaia rising to its mosque

entries.caption: Why Algeria
entries.description: The Roman cities of Tunisia, the Sahara of Libya and the Atlas of Morocco, with almost nobody in them.
entries.subject: a lone traveller looking out over the Grand Erg from a dune
